Read initially as a within-subject condition manipulation because all 194 ids appear under all 7 group values -- but only 12 items actually repeat, always across the same two groups (Feeling Heard + Respect), for all 194 ids, and the responses NEVER disagree. group is a subscale label, not a condition, and those 12 items belong to two subscales, so each response was emitted once per subscale. CORRECTED 2026-09-02. Every id+item occurs exactly twice -- never three or four times -- with an identical resp and zero conflicts anywhere (density 1.99 in metadata.csv). This was first read as one twin's data emitted twice with the co-twin's data lost, on the reasoning that twins cannot agree on 100% of items. The id counts refute that: florida_twins_behavior_cads holds 1,378 distinct ids against the separately-processed florida_twins_cads's 1,272 on the identical 57 items, so it is not missing half its sample -- it has more people, not fewer. The uniform 2x is consistent with the double-entry layout standard in twin research, where each pair contributes two rows so each twin is once the target and once the co-twin; data/florida_twins_behavior.R bind_rows() the bg_id0 and bg_id1 arms of that layout, which reproduces every person twice. A plain dedupe is correct and nothing needs regenerating. Verify the id count is UNCHANGED afterwards, not doubled.

138,035 repeated id+item pairs, up to 4 copies each, and ZERO of them disagree on resp. Dedupe, and populate treat consistently. Worth confirming at the source whether the five rbinded frames are genuinely distinct waves: if they are, the wave column should be carried through AS WELL, but it is not what is causing this flag.
